items.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: no one can beat Freddie Green on that... when you get a chance listen to Basie

ctx.x: The lower strings. So on the other fingers he would sort of just deaden the other strings or you just don’t hit them?

You can deaden them. You deaden them. But it gives you that nice — without that with Basie, I mean no one can beat Freddie Green on that. But now that’s a different — when you get a chance listen to Basie, then listen to Johnny Mathis with Tony. It’s a little different. Tony’s was more, you can hear the change more. And it’s just fabulous with Tony. I think he used an L5 I’m pretty sure, where on Basie, I think he used a Gretsch, I think he played a Gretsch guitar, a big body Gretsch.
